title: O-map/way method-site: Sampling method for plant site inventories in forests
author: André Strauss
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.6xhhfj6

steps.title: Prepare Navigation and Recording Tools
steps.instruction: Equip yourself with an orienteering map or similar quality map (paper or electronic, ideally 1:5,000 scale), GPS, compass, and recording devices.

steps.title: Conduct Seasonal Inspection Rounds
steps.instruction: Perform 3 complete inspection rounds in the forest target area within a single year during the season when the target plant species are most recognizable. Ideally, these rounds should be carried out by different persons.

steps.title: Screen Sites Along Accessible Ways
steps.instruction: Screen for plant sites along all accessible ways in the target area, recording the location via GPS (and optionally sketching on the map), noting site area sizes, plant abundance, and optionally the plant state.

substeps.instruction: Limit recording distance from the way to 3 m for herbaceous plants.
Limit recording distance from the way to 10 m for shrubs at least 1 m high.
Limit recording distance from the way to 20 m for trees at least 2 m high and any species clearly recognizable from the way.
Sketch the inspection track on the orienteering map.

steps.title: Screen Sites via Meandering Loops
steps.instruction: Search for new sites in accessible subareas between ways and other visible lines on the map or in nature using 5-20 m broad meandering loops.

substeps.instruction: Exclude sites already recorded during the way-screening process.
Record site locations and notes using the same method as used for sites along ways.
